brief_item.title: GPUSparse：GPU加速稀疏检索实现235倍加速
brief_item.direction_name: 芯片内存接口、数据搬移与软硬件协同
brief_item.core_conclusion: GPUSparse通过GPU并行倒排索引和批量scatter-add评分算法，在880万文档上实现235倍加速，达到787 QPS吞吐。
brief_item.mechanism: 采用块对齐warp合并posting列表和批量scatter-add内核，单次处理数百查询。
brief_item.result: 相比Pyserini CPU实现加速235倍至9.6ms，文档并行内核达62.6%峰值HBM带宽。
brief_item.boundary: 单查询9.6ms高于CPU近似搜索，批次500需44GB显存。
brief_item.project_relevance: 展示H100上带宽受限稀疏检索模式，权衡是根本设计选择。

facts.title: GPUSparse: GPU-Accelerated Learned Sparse Retrieval with Parallel Inverted Indices
facts.event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-06-24 on GPU-accelerated exact learned sparse retrieval using parallel inverted indices
facts.problem: Learned sparse retrieval models (SPLADE) achieve quality competitive with dense models while preserving interpretability, but inference-time scoring relies on CPU-bound inverted index traversal algorithms (WAND, Block-Max WAND). This creates a fundamental bottleneck for real-time serving at scale. Existing GPU sparse retrieval systems (Seismic) trade 25% recall for speed.
facts.mechanism: GPUSparse introduces: (1) GPU-parallel inverted index with block-aligned, warp-coalesced posting lists, (2) batched scatter-add scoring algorithm processing hundreds of queries simultaneously, (3) fused Triton kernels. The scatter-add kernel processes only O(q_bar * L_bar) entries per query (query terms × posting lists). A document-parallel kernel trades work-efficiency for bandwidth utilization.

evidence.claim: 235x speedup over Pyserini CPU exact scoring at 8.8M documents
evidence.condition: MS MARCO passage ranking 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB

evidence.claim: Achieves 787 QPS throughput at 8.8M documents with batch 500
evidence.condition: MS MARCO 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB, exact scoring

evidence.claim: Document-parallel kernel achieves 62.6% of H100 peak HBM bandwidth
evidence.condition: 100K documents, CSR index by document

evidence.claim: Scatter-add kernel achieves 12.5 GB/s effective bandwidth (0.37% of peak) due to scattered atomic writes
evidence.condition: 100K documents, work-efficient design

evidence.claim: 8.5 GB for inverted index at 8.8M passages (11% of 80GB H100)
evidence.condition: MS MARCO 8.8M passages, SPLADE embeddings

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on MS MARCO passage ranking (8.8M passages) with real SPLADE embeddings. Hardware: H100 80GB GPU. Metrics include MRR@10, Recall@1000, per-query latency, QPS throughput. Cross-domain validation on BEIR benchmarks (SciFact, NFCorpus, TREC-COVID). Comparison against Pyserini CPU exact scoring, Seismic (fastest CPU sparse), cuSPARSE SpMV, and dense matmul ground truth.
facts.limitations: GPU cost: H100 GPU is substantially more expensive than CPU-only retrieval. Single-query latency 9.6ms at 8.8M docs - CPU methods faster for single-query approximate search. Score buffer memory scales as O(B*N): 44GB at batch 500 with 8.8M docs (55% of H100). No dynamic updates without full index rebuild. 6x slower than Seismic for approximate top-10 retrieval at 8.8M.
facts.project_relevance: GPUSparse demonstrates memory-bandwidth-bound sparse retrieval on H100 with 62.6% peak utilization achieved via document-parallel kernel. The work-efficiency vs bandwidth-efficiency tradeoff is fundamental: scatter-add processes only query-relevant postings (work-efficient) at 0.37% bandwidth utilization, while doc-parallel achieves 62.6% peak but reads 76GB vs 0.09GB per batch. The 8.5GB index size at 8.8M passages shows sparse format memory advantage vs dense (~1TB). Index cannot be updated without full rebuild - limitation for dynamic workloads.

brief_item.title: 状态绑定证据防止Agent修复循环破坏正确性
brief_item.core_conclusion: Agent代码修复循环中正确率从首次修订后的0.820降至二次修订后的0.673，16%轨迹丢失正确补丁。
brief_item.mechanism: 状态绑定类型修订合约将验证器证据绑定到精确代码状态并保留验证检查点。
brief_item.result: 过期trace使34/135正确起点受损，正确率0.820降至0.673。
brief_item.boundary: 限于HumanEval修复与强制修订协议，未证改进修复能力。
brief_item.project_relevance: 证明过期反馈损害正确起点22.2个百分点，状态绑定证据方法可为工具调用复用提供状态一致性保证。

facts.title: Looping Is Not Reliability: State-Bound Evidence and Typed Revision Contracts for Agentic Code Repair
facts.event_hint: AgenticDev 2026 study on correctness regression in agentic code repair loops
facts.problem: Generate-test-revise loops in coding agents provide no reliability guarantee; correct patches can be destroyed in subsequent revisions, stale observations can revive old bugs, and correlated verifiers can confirm the same error
facts.mechanism: State-bound typed revision contract that binds verifier evidence to exact code states, preserves verified checkpoints, and emits auditable admission receipts; separates admission, preservation, grounded certification, competence, and liveness

evidence.claim: Current correctness falls from 0.820 after one revision to 0.673 after two revisions
evidence.condition: Forced revision protocol, current traces, 30 HumanEval repairs, 900 three-revision trajectories
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, Figure 1b discussion

evidence.claim: Ever-correct rate rises to 0.847 despite current correctness decline
evidence.condition: Cumulative discovery metric, 30 HumanEval repairs, three-revision trajectories
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, Figure 1b discussion

evidence.claim: Stale traces harm 34/135 correct starts versus 4/135 with current traces, a 22.2-point increase
evidence.condition: 14B model replication, prespecified study, task-cluster 95% CI [8.9, 37.0], exact Holm p=0.0337
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5, Results section, RQ2 discussion

evidence.claim: 16.0% of trajectories produce correct patch then lose it by revision 3
evidence.condition: 30 HumanEval repairs, forced revision protocol

evidence.claim: Reference implementation is executable specification, not evidence of improved repair competence
evidence.condition: Post-study implementation; not used to generate empirical results

facts.evaluation_context: Sealed five-seed study over 30 HumanEval repairs producing 900 three-revision trajectories. Two common-state studies use 2,430 branches from identical frozen programs to remove post-treatment risk-set bias. Prespecified 14B replication with 135 starts per condition. Repository experiments over 24 bugs and four coder stacks (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct-AWQ, Qwen3-Coder-Next-FP8, Devstral Small 2 24B). Reference implementation developed after empirical study completed.
facts.limitations: Study scoped to HumanEval repair under forced-revision protocol; does not show adaptive loops must regress but demonstrates need for preservation and stopping rules. Repository experiments exposed floor effects and component heterogeneity without Holm-significant effects. Reference implementation is executable specification for contract enforcement, not evidence of improved repair competence or calibrated verifier dependence.
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to agent acceleration project questions on whether parallel tool calls or caching introduce correctness risk. Demonstrates that stale feedback harms correct starts (22.2-point increase in harm). State-bound evidence binding suggests approach for ensuring tool-call reuse and read results are tied to exact code states. However, limited to code repair domain; direct applicability to read/grep acceleration unclear.

_provenance.source_title: Looping Is Not Reliability: State-Bound Evidence and Typed Revision Contracts for Agentic Code Repair

brief_item.title: ReCo奖励协调KV压缩实现2.08-2.35倍推理加速
brief_item.direction_name: 压缩、增量传输、预取与放置
brief_item.core_conclusion: ReCo通过奖励自适应KV缓存压缩和反思token惩罚，在六个推理基准上实现2.08-2.35倍加速。
brief_item.mechanism: 奖励协调三个组件：高奖励步更激进压缩、反思token带惩罚、基于置信度早停。
brief_item.result: 生成token减37%至65%，显存28.78GB降至17.92GB，准确率60.2%对58.1%。
brief_item.boundary: 仅数学推理基准，组件开销约4%，需大步级奖励估计。
brief_item.project_relevance: 奖励自适应压缩机制显示压缩容忍度沿推理链变化，token减少37-65%直接降低跨域传输带宽需求。

facts.title: Fewer Tokens, Smaller Cache: Reward-Coordinated Efficient Reasoning
facts.event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-08-05 on efficient LLM reasoning via reward-coordinated KV-cache compression and generation control
facts.problem: Large Reasoning Models use long chain-of-thought reasoning which causes overthinking and high inference costs. Existing KV-cache compression methods apply uniform policies across the trajectory and ignore that compression tolerance varies along reasoning steps. Cache-only compression can backfire by lengthening generation, partially canceling intended savings.
facts.mechanism: ReCo coordinates three components under a single process reward: (1) reward-adaptive KV-cache compression that shrinks cache harder at high-reward steps, (2) reward-banded penalty on reflection tokens to curb redundant generation, (3) confidence-based early stopping triggered when answer perplexity satisfies threshold. A lightweight process-reward estimator scores each completed step.

evidence.claim: ReCo achieves 2.08x-2.35x latency speedup over Full CoT across three reasoning models
evidence.condition: single NVIDIA H20 GPU, six reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, AMC, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA)

evidence.claim: ReCo reduces generated tokens by 37%-65% across models
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen3-8B on six benchmarks

evidence.claim: ReCo uses 17.92GB peak GPU memory, a 37.7% reduction over full cache
evidence.condition: AIME25 benchmark, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, single H20 GPU

evidence.claim: ReCo achieves 60.2% average accuracy vs. 58.1% baseline at comparable latency
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, six-benchmark average, 26.88s latency vs. 28.29s baseline

evidence.claim: Cache-only baselines gain only modest speedups (1.09-1.33x) since inflated generation cancels per-token attention savings
evidence.condition: Llama-8B, cache-only compression methods (SnapKV, R-KV, RPC)

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on three reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen3-8B) across six math benchmarks from grade-school to competition level. Hardware: single NVIDIA H20 GPU. Metrics include accuracy, average tokens per problem, end-to-end wall-clock latency per problem, peak GPU memory.
facts.limitations: Evaluation limited to math reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, AMC, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA). ReCo components add small overhead: Pilot scoring 0.60%, KV compression 0.11%, reflection penalty 1.24%, early stopping 1.98% of end-to-end time. Uses a 30M step-level reward estimator.
facts.project_relevance: KV-cache compression is directly relevant to cross-domain transmission of reasoning model states. Reward-adaptive compression based on trajectory position suggests that compression tolerance varies along reasoning chain. Token reduction (37%-65%) translates to reduced transfer bandwidth. Memory reduction (17.92GB vs 28.78GB) affects cross-domain cache placement capacity. The mechanism shows how step-wise importance metrics (process reward) can guide compression policy, which could inform cross-domain cache selection and transfer prioritization.

_provenance.source_title: Fewer Tokens, Smaller Cache: Reward-Coordinated Efficient Reasoning

brief_item.title: 编程式工具调用在JSON失效时保持100%准确率
brief_item.core_conclusion: 编程式工具调用通过Python类型存根在单次推理turn中执行，13/14模型上匹配或超越JSON工具调用。
brief_item.mechanism: 工具暴露为Python类型存根，单次agent轮次内经shell子进程执行并取结果。
brief_item.result: GPT-5.6系列在BFCL v4提升10.6%，高fan-out编程式保100%而JSON全丢。
brief_item.boundary: BFCL v4仅测参数序列化精度，编程式有1.5倍token开销。
brief_item.project_relevance: 单轮代码调用替多轮JSON降链式延迟，但不减Read与Grep操作。

facts.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
facts.event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-08-06 comparing programmatic tool calling to JSON tool calling across 14 models on BFCL v4
facts.problem: Tool-calling agents emit structured JSON objects for each function call, requiring precise argument serialization, multi-step chaining, and fan-out across heterogeneous APIs. For code-capable models, JSON format is a design choice not a necessity. Whether programmatic tool calling matches JSON tool calling across model families and adversarial context loads remained untested.
facts.mechanism: Programmatic tool calling (PTC) exposes tools as typed Python stubs that the model invokes through code, with execution and results handled in a single agent turn via shell subprocess. The agent loop executes the script without additional inference turns. JSON tool calling requires separate inference turns per function call.

evidence.claim: GPT-5.6 family achieves 10.6% improvement over JSON tool calling baseline on BFCL v4
evidence.condition: BFCL v4 subset (309 entries, eight categories)

evidence.claim: Programmatic tool calling matches or exceeds baseline in 13 of 14 models under parallel fan-out
evidence.condition: Parallel fan-out testing, Claude Sonnet 5 N=100 maintains 100% enumeration accuracy vs. 0% for JSON

evidence.claim: JSON tool calling drops tool calls entirely at N=70-72 (Claude Sonnet 5)
evidence.condition: Claude Sonnet 5, enumeration task

evidence.claim: Programmatic tool calling holds stable under context rot while JSON tool calling degrades 2.3% on average
evidence.condition: Context flood (128 schemas) vs filtered (relevant only), n=31 per condition

evidence.claim: Chaining entries complete in 0.32-0.96 of baseline latency for 13 of 14 models
evidence.condition: Sequential chaining tasks, single inference turn vs. two turns for JSON

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on BFCL v4 subset (309 entries, eight categories: simple_python, multiple, parallel, parallel multiple, live_simple, live_multiple, live_parallel, live parallel multiple). 14 models tested (5 Anthropic: Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, 4.6, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5; 9 OpenAI: GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5-nano, GPT-5, GPT-5.4-mini, 5.4, 5.6-Luna/ Sol/Terra). Ab studies: fan-out enumeration, chaining, context rot (filtered vs. 128-schema flood).
facts.limitations: BFCL v4 uses echo-return stubs (returns arguments verbatim, not real API calls) - measures argument serialization accuracy, not end-to-end tool-use correctness. Ablation entry counts small (n=31-52 per condition) with wide confidence intervals. 20% evaluator-human misalignment found in BFCL v4's LLM-judge mode (deterministic scorer avoids this). Programmatic tool calling has 1.5x input token overhead vs JSON on chaining. Results may not transfer to settings where return values affect downstream calls.
facts.project_relevance: Programmatic tool calling reduces agent tool execution latency by eliminating per-call inference turns (0.32-0.96x chaining latency). Maintains 100% accuracy under high fan-out (N=100) where JSON tool calling fails entirely. Robust under context flooding (+5.5% vs. -2.3% degradation). For Agent semantic acceleration, this addresses tool call overhead specifically but does not directly reduce Read/Grep/repository search operations. The method is relevant for optimizing tool execution chains in agents, particularly for parallel operations and chaining scenarios. However, the paper does not report Read次数, Grep次数, token consumption beyond input overhead, or task success rates beyond BFCL accuracy.
source_notes: Authors from PwC Commercial Technology and Innovation Office
